### Observed differences

- In both windows, every case contains A22, A23 and A24 (their profiles have full support, 200 of 200 cases, in each window). In the earlier window, each case additionally executed exactly one of three mutually exclusive alternatives: A14 in about 32 in 100 cases, A15 in about 28 in 100 and A20 in about 40 in 100 — the shares sum to one, and no case contained two of them. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, REL001, REL002, REL006, DIR004, DIR005, POS004, POS005]
- That alternative step always sat between A22 and A24, in one of two placements: directly after A22 and before A23 (about 45 in 100 earlier cases; A22's outgoing transitions went to A20 in about 21%, A14 in about 14% and A15 in about 11% of cases), or directly after A23 and before A24 (about 55 in 100 cases; A23 led to one of the three in about 54% of its outgoing transitions). Both placements occurred for each of the three alternatives. [DIR004, DIR005, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, LAG001, LAG003, REL004, REL008, REL011]
- In the later window, none of the three alternatives was observed: participation fell from 64, 56 and 80 of 200 cases to zero, mean occurrences per case fell to zero, and no outgoing transitions from A14, A15 or A20 were recorded. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, POS001, POS002, POS003]
- As a result, the remaining chain became direct: A22 led only to A23 (100% of its outgoing transitions, previously about 55%) and A23 led only to A24 (100%, previously about 46%); A23 immediately followed A22 in every later case (previously about 55 in 100, with a one-step gap in the rest), A24 immediately followed A23 in every later case (previously about 45 in 100), and the distance from A22 to A24 shortened from three steps in every earlier case to two steps in every later case. [DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG003, LAG002]
- The relational picture matches: each alternative co-occurred with A22, A23 and A24 in roughly 28–40 in 100 earlier cases and in no later case, while the alternatives never co-occurred with each other in either window. [REL003, REL004, REL005, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL001, REL002, REL006]
- The surviving activities barely moved within the trace: A22's mean relative position shifted from about 0.46 to 0.47 and A24's from about 0.57 to 0.55, consistent with one intermediate step disappearing rather than any relocation. [POS004, POS005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the process step carried by A14, A15 and A20 — a set of mutually exclusive alternatives of which exactly one executed per case, placed either between A22 and A23 or between A23 and A24 — was no longer executed in the later window, so that cases ran A22 → A23 → A24 directly. The signs are direct and consistent: participation of all three alternatives fell from 28–40 in 100 cases to zero out of 200; their outgoing transitions disappeared while A22 and A23 became exclusively sequential; and the A22-to-A24 distance shortened from three steps to two. The volume of qualifying evidence also exceeds what an unchanged process produces: 28 control-flow items qualified where about 0.39 were expected by chance, and all of them describe this one coherent difference rather than scattered unrelated ones. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

Limitations: zero participation strictly establishes only that the alternatives were not executed in the observed later cases; the evidence cannot distinguish a permanent removal of the step from it being skipped in every observed case under conditions absent from the sample, nor show whether the work was dropped or absorbed into the neighbouring activities. The many agreeing items largely restate a single trace-level difference and should not be read as independent confirmations. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, LAG002]
